Pkgdown setup

Source: PKGDOWN.md

These instructions are for Joie or another repository maintainer setting up the evaluatr package website.

One-time setup

  1. Install R (version 4.1 or newer) and the package dependencies.

  2. Install the website tools in R:

    install.packages(c("devtools", "pkgdown"))

  3. In GitHub, open Settings > Actions > General and make sure actions are allowed to run. Under Workflow permissions, select Read and write permissions, then save. This is required because the pkgdown workflow creates or updates the gh-pages branch.

  4. Push the repository to GitHub and push at least one commit to main. The workflow in .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml runs automatically and creates the gh-pages branch if it does not already exist. It then publishes the generated site there.

  5. After the first workflow run succeeds, open Settings > Pages for the repository and configure:

    • Source: Deploy from a branch
    • Branch: gh-pages
    • Folder: / (root)

    If gh-pages is not listed yet, wait for the workflow to finish and refresh the page. Save the setting. The site URL is: https://joieensor.github.io/evaluatr/.

Preview the site locally

From the package root, run:

devtools::document()
pkgdown::build_site()

The generated site is written to docs/. Open docs/index.html in a browser to inspect the result. To preview while editing, use:

pkgdown::preview_site()

Do not edit generated files in docs/ directly. Change _pkgdown.yml, the README, vignettes, or roxygen comments under R/, then rebuild the site.

Publish an update

  1. Check the site locally with pkgdown::build_site().
  2. Commit the source changes, including _pkgdown.yml and any documentation source files.
  3. Push the commit to main.
  4. Open the repository’s Actions tab and monitor the pkgdown workflow.
  5. After it succeeds, allow a minute or two for GitHub Pages to update.

The workflow installs the package and its website dependencies, rebuilds the site, and publishes the result to gh-pages. A failed build usually contains the exact R or pkgdown error in the workflow log.

Common fixes

  • If pkgdown reports topics missing from the reference index, add the topic to the appropriate reference group in _pkgdown.yml, or mark genuinely internal documentation with @keywords internal.
  • If a new function or dataset is absent, run devtools::document() before rebuilding the site.
  • Keep public authors and ORCID identifiers in DESCRIPTION. The authors page is generated from package metadata and should not be treated as the source of truth.
  • If the workflow cannot install a dependency, check DESCRIPTION and make sure the dependency is under Imports, Suggests, or Config/Needs/website as appropriate.
